reasoning: Niche Reels are the only format that distributes (53–104 reach for the best body and psychology posts), so this is a Reel. To keep the hook experiment balanced: the last four posts used list and direct-claim hooks, so this one uses the 'What X does to your body' style. It sticks to the human-body niche but adds an extreme, high-stakes setting (Everest's death zone), which should cut the skip rate the way the cold-water and fear reels did. The final slide uses the follow-tease CTA, part of the follow-conversion experiment. This is also the first Trial Reel. With 0 followers, all reach is from non-followers anyway, so it tests whether trial distribution behaves differently at almost no risk. Documentary music fits the tone. Palette 2 continues the rotation.
topic: Everest death zone: low oxygen, no acclimatization, thick blood, brain swelling, record-low blood oxygen
hook: What the death zone does to your body

slides.title: Above 8,000 meters
slides.body: Climbers call it the death zone. Air pressure is about a third of sea level, so each breath brings far less oxygen.
slides.image_prompt: Snow-covered Himalayan summit ridge at dawn, thin clouds below, empty oxygen cylinder lying in the snow, cold blue light
slides.credit:
Debasish biswas kolkata
Derivative work MagentaGreen (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

slides.title: Your body can't adapt
slides.body: Up there, nobody can fully acclimatize. The body slowly breaks down, losing weight and muscle the longer it stays.
slides.image_prompt: Lone orange tent on a windswept icy slope at extreme altitude, snow blowing across, dark sky above

slides.title: Blood turns thick
slides.body: The body makes extra red blood cells to carry oxygen. Thicker blood raises the risk of clots and strokes.
slides.image_prompt: Dense cluster of red blood cells crowding inside a narrow vessel, dramatic microscopic view, deep red tones

slides.title: Fluid floods the brain
slides.body: Low oxygen can make vessels leak. Fluid in the brain or lungs can kill within hours unless climbers descend.
slides.image_prompt: Anatomical brain model encased in frost on a snowy rock, cold mist around it, high mountain background

slides.title: Blood oxygen hits bottom
slides.body: Blood samples taken near Everest's summit showed oxygen levels about 75% below normal, among the lowest ever recorded in humans.
slides.image_prompt: Glass blood sample vial standing in snow on a mountain summit, jagged peaks and thin blue sky behind

cta: Follow so you don't miss tomorrow's fact
caption:
Above 8,000 meters, the human body starts dying slowly. In 2007, doctors drew blood from climbers near Everest's summit. Their oxygen levels were among the lowest ever measured in living people.

The body can't adapt up there. Blood thickens, fluid can leak into the brain, and climbers lose muscle by the day. Most summit pushes are a race against the clock. Save this for the next time someone calls Everest 'just a long hike.'

Follow for one fact your brain won't believe, every day. Would you ever try to climb Everest?
